groups.shared_idea: Probability of 'at least one' when choosing without replacement, solved as 1 - C(no-success group, k)/C(total, k) (committee with >=1 junior; product of two picks is even = 1 - P(both odd)).
groups.why: Identical complement-with-combinations method; only the context differs. 016 is the more standard ACT framing.

groups.shared_idea: Expected net gain of a game of chance: sum of payoff x probability, accounting for losses or cost.
groups.why: Same setup (a game with payoffs and probabilities) and same one-line expected-value computation.

groups.shared_idea: Multiply/divide numbers in scientific notation by combining coefficients and adding/subtracting powers of 10.
groups.why: Same bare computation type; 189 also covers squaring and negative exponents, so it subsumes 019.

groups.shared_idea: Line through a given point parallel/perpendicular to a line given in standard form; find slope from standard form, write point-slope, then find an intercept.
groups.why: Identical pipeline; the perpendicular version adds the negative reciprocal, so 034 covers more.

groups.shared_idea: Given a point (a, b) on y = f(x), find the image point on a transformed graph g(x) = A f(Bx + C) + D.
groups.why: Same 'track one point through transformations' method; 122 adds stretch and reflection, so it covers 021.

groups.shared_idea: Simplify a monomial with rational exponents using power-of-a-power and product rules.
groups.why: Same exponent-rule simplification; 153 adds a second variable and a negative fractional power.

groups.shared_idea: Space diagonal of a rectangular box/cube: d = sqrt(l^2 + w^2 + h^2).
groups.why: 074 runs the formula backward (diagonal to side to volume), but the key idea is the same.

groups.shared_idea: Rewrite a shifted exponential b^(x+k) as b^k * b^x.
groups.why: 172 adds one subtraction step; the core insight (f(x+k) = b^k f(x)) is identical.

groups.shared_idea: Quadratic in a known form (vertex or factored) with one unknown coefficient a: substitute a given point to get a, then evaluate.
groups.why: Same 'plug a point to find a, then evaluate' method; 022 also needs symmetry to locate the vertex.

groups.shared_idea: Combine two groups by adding totals: (total1 + total2)/(count1 + count2), not averaging the two rates/means.
groups.why: Merged population density is a weighted mean in different clothing; the same trap (averaging 2,500 and 2,000) applies.

groups.shared_idea: Worker-time units: compute the rate per worker per unit time and scale (painter-hours, hen-days).
groups.why: Both rely on the 'per worker per unit time' rate; 097 adds a mid-job change.

groups.shared_idea: Relative speed: time = separation distance / combined (or difference of) speeds.
groups.why: Catch-up (subtract speeds) and opposite-direction meeting on a track (add speeds) use the same relative-speed idea.

groups.shared_idea: Number of solutions of linear equations/systems determined by matching coefficients (proportional or equal coefficients).
groups.why: Both ask for a parameter value that makes coefficients match (infinitely many solutions vs. no solution).

groups.shared_idea: Factor numerator and denominator of rational expressions and cancel common factors.
groups.why: 170 is the same factor-and-cancel process with one extra multiplication.

groups.shared_idea: Area of an isosceles triangle/trapezoid: drop an altitude, use a Pythagorean triple (5-12-13 or 3-4-5) to get the height, then use the area formula.
groups.why: Same altitude-plus-Pythagorean-triple method on an isosceles figure.

groups.shared_idea: Area of an equilateral triangle, s^2*sqrt(3)/4 (the hexagon is 6 such triangles).
groups.why: The hexagon problem is the equilateral-area problem times 6.

groups.shared_idea: Geometric probability as (target region area)/(total area), where the target region is a difference of two similar shapes (square frame; annulus).
groups.why: Same 'outer minus inner area over total' method.

groups.shared_idea: Successive percent changes multiply as factors and do not add (1.2 x 0.75; 0.8 x ? = 1).
groups.why: Same multiplicative-factor idea and the same trap answer; 127 solves for the second factor instead of the product.

groups.shared_idea: Find the whole from a known percent of it (0.85x = 68; 0.15x = 27), then use the whole.
groups.why: Same 'divide by the percent to recover the base' step.

groups.shared_idea: Chain two ratios through a shared middle term (a:b and b:c to a:b:c) by scaling to a common value of b.
groups.why: Same chaining technique; 176 adds a part-to-total step.

groups.shared_idea: Area unit conversion uses the square of the linear factor (sq ft to sq yd: /9; m^2 to cm^2: x10,000).
groups.why: Same squared-conversion-factor idea; 067 adds rounding up.

groups.shared_idea: Cut a figure with a line/plane parallel to its base: the small similar piece scales by k^2 (area) or k^3 (volume); the remaining piece = whole - small.
groups.why: Same 'similar piece cut off by a parallel cut, subtract from whole' method in 2-D vs 3-D.

groups.shared_idea: Unit price = cost / quantity, compared or converted to a per-ounce price.
groups.why: 151 is the same unit-price computation with a pounds-to-ounces conversion.

groups.shared_idea: Standard deviation measures spread from the mean: values far from the mean raise it, values at the mean lower it.
groups.why: Both are conceptual SD questions answered by the same 'distance from the mean' intuition, with no computation.

groups.shared_idea: Solve a one-variable linear equation (f(a) = 20 is just 5 - 3a = 20).
groups.why: Both are basic linear solves; a student would see them as the same item. 030 (with fractions) is related but needs clearing denominators.
